A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FCMR and CMRGen. All 27 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations on FCMR, image-removal experiments on MMQA and FCMR, and statement-level and manually annotated error analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds task-optimization experiments in Table 5 and reasoning-model evaluations in Table 9.

M1.justification: Section 6.3 adds preliminary inference adaptations: chart captioning and table linearization, explicit four-stage reasoning prompts, and Self-Refine. These extend the evaluated procedures while retaining the main CMRGen pipeline and existing DePlot approach.

E1.justification: FCMR's financial tasks and MMQA evaluation coverage are retained. Material-CMR's construction example already appears in both appendices. The new experiments use existing Hard questions; MME-Finance is discussed only as related work.

E2.justification: V2 Table 9 adds a distinct comparison group of reasoning-oriented models: Mulberry-LLaVA-8B, Virgo 72B, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking, and o1, alongside a Claude baseline. This substantially extends comparator coverage beyond v1's standard MLLM and DePlot comparisons, whose membership is retained.

E3.justification: New experiments evaluate prompting and input-conversion configurations on 100 Hard cases. Table 9 explicitly uses 100 randomly selected Hard samples because of model costs. These are additional subset protocols; the original full-benchmark sample counts, accuracy metric, and zero-shot evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Table 5 adds a cumulative component analysis of modality integration, four-stage prompting, and self-refinement. Figure 9 compares baseline and optimized reasoning trajectories. Existing error analyses remain, including chart interpretability, which moves from Section 6.2 to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: Existing results match, including v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 3. V2 adds Claude's 32%, 39%, 42%, and 46% across Table 5 configurations; Table 9 reports Mulberry 12%, Virgo 19%, Gemini Thinking 39%, and o1 43%. Figure 9 adds improved stage-survival results. These are new subset results, not revisions to full-benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The task definitions and four reasoning stages are retained. Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs, and using the existing stages in a new prompt introduces no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, retaining the benchmark contribution, three-hop difficulty, Claude's 30.4% accuracy, and the information-retrieval bottleneck. The introduction and conclusion preserve these central contributions; the additional experiments supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V1's prospective prompt-optimization discussion is replaced by interpretations that the tested interventions reduce retrieval and reasoning failures and 'saturate' at 46% accuracy. V2 also softens the manual-analysis limitation and emphasizes its value. The chart-interpretability explanations are retained in Appendix E.

D1.justification: Figures 25–27 newly provide chart-captioning, four-stage reasoning, and self-refinement prompts. V2 identifies manual analysts as in-house researchers. Section 3.2 now calls human review optional, while Appendix C.1 still states all Hard instances were reviewed, leaving the procedure less clear without establishing an actual dataset change.

R1.justification: V2 adds MME-Finance to Section 2.1 and Table 1, plus supporting references for financial MLLMs, modality integration, self-refinement, and reasoning models. These are targeted extensions; the central positioning against MMQA remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 condenses parts of the introduction and error discussion, moves chart interpretability to Appendix E, adds Section 6.3, and revises the limitations. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5 and 9, Figure 9, and prompt Figures 25–27. It adds a row to Table 1, relocates v1's contamination Table 3 to appendix Table 8, and resizes several existing diagrams. The existing visual designs and plotted results are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: V2 turns v1's proposed prompt optimization into a documented preliminary experiment and adds reasoning-model comparisons, making the benchmark's diagnostic findings more useful. The gains are limited by evaluation on 100 Hard cases without uncertainty estimates and by the unreconciled human-review descriptions in Section 3.2 and Appendix C.1.
